review_notes: I read the whole target file and compared it with sibling files. The sibling files were `Algebra/Bialgebra/Quotient.lean`, `Algebra/UnitriangularStageCoordinateRing.lean`, `Algebra/UnitriangularStageCoordinates.lean` and `GroupScheme/UpperTriangularSplitKernel.lean`. I also checked Mathlib for `AlgHom.cancel_right`. The one substantive duplication is the counit/comultiplication verification for a bialgebra structure on an algebra map out of a Hopf quotient. It appears in `unitriangularStageSuccessorBialgHom` here and in `bialgHomOfCompQuotient` in `UpperTriangularSplitKernel.lean`. A third, generic version exists in `Bialgebra.Quotient.counitAlgHom_comp_liftₐ` and `map_liftₐ_comp_comulAlgHom`. My grep found no uses of those two lemmas anywhere in the formal-frontier tree. The other repeated patterns in this file are short: the `hfactor` rfl, the `Over.OverMorphism.ext` + `Spec.map_comp` + `congr 1` point lemmas, and the identical `map_id`/`map_comp` blocks. I judged these too small to report. I did not check whether the `IsCoideal` instance needed for the unused `Bialgebra.Quotient` lemmas can be found for `ideal K n r`, and I did not check how the lemma elaborates when `successor` is unfolded to `liftₐ`. The proposed lemma is untested. It avoids those issues by working with a surjective bialgebra map and `AlgHom.cancel_right`.

findings.problem: This proof checks, by hand and by cancelling the quotient map, that an algebra map `f : A⧸I →ₐ B` with `f ∘ q = target` (target a bialgebra map) preserves counit and comultiplication. The same argument is written again in `bialgHomOfCompQuotient` in `UpperTriangularSplitKernel.lean`. The only differences are the types. Both proofs use `Ideal.Quotient.algHom_ext`, `counitAlgHom_comp` on the target and on the quotient, `map_comp_comulAlgHom`, and `Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp`. Both also use several long `change` statements. The repo already has generic `Bialgebra.Quotient.counitAlgHom_comp_liftₐ` and `map_liftₐ_comp_comulAlgHom`, but nothing uses them. So there are now three versions of the same reasoning.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one generic lemma or def next to the `Bialgebra.Quotient` lemmas. Statement: for bialgebras `A B C` over a commutative ring `R`, a surjective bialgebra map `q : A →ₐc[R] B`, a bialgebra map `target : A →ₐc[R] C`, and `f : B →ₐ[R] C` with `f.comp q = target.toAlgHom`, we get `BialgHom.ofAlgHom f _ _ : B →ₐc[R] C`. Proof sketch:
- Counit: apply `(AlgHom.cancel_right hq_surj).mp` and use `f ∘ q = target` with `counitAlgHom_comp` for `target` and for `q`.
- Comul: apply `AlgHom.cancel_right` again. Rewrite with `← map_comp_comulAlgHom q`, `← Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp` and the factorization hypothesis, then close with `map_comp_comulAlgHom target`.
The surjectivity hypothesis can also be replaced by `Ideal.Quotient.algHom_ext`.
Use in this file: `unitriangularStageSuccessorBialgHom K n r := bialgHomOfCompSurj (quotientBialgHom K n r) (quotientBialgHom K n (r+1)) (successor K n r) rfl`, with `Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective` for the surjectivity argument. The existing `rfl` (`hfactor`) supplies the factorization hypothesis.
Use in `UpperTriangularSplitKernel`: `bialgHomOfCompQuotient` becomes a one-line specialization with `q := upperTriangularQuotientBialgHom K n`. The two derived defs there (`upperTriangularDiagonalSectionBialgHom` and `upperTriangularUnitriangularBialgHom`) are unchanged.
To make the file import the lemma, add `public import AlgebraicGroups.Algebra.Bialgebra.Quotient` or the new generic file here. The target file currently relies on the transitive import only.
findings.benefit: The roughly 30-line counit/comul argument is stated and checked once instead of being copied for each quotient. `unitriangularStageSuccessorBialgHom` shrinks to a single application, so the file keeps its scheme-level content. Later stage or quotient maps can reuse the lemma instead of repeating long `change` blocks. The currently unused generic quotient lemmas in `Bialgebra/Quotient.lean` can either be reused by the new lemma or removed.

lemma cancel_right {g₁ g₂ : B →ₐ[R] C} {f : A →ₐ[R] B} (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
